scope: Investigation only: local ARM64 fresh test wikis; no optimization deployed. Normal provisioner restored after temporary read-only instrumentation.
method: hrtime markers at PHP entry, updater execute, dependencies, core updates, extension registration/updates, post-update maintenance; hrtime around Database::doSingleStatementQuery; per-callback updater timers. Three sequential fresh form-created wikis, one private.
limits: SQL elapsed includes client/server round trip, not server CPU time.
Timings vary with cache warmth and host load. Instrumentation adds some overhead.
SQL fingerprints hash text without database identity; matching text across passes does not prove all repeated statements address the same database.
Updater callback applied counters follow upstream return values and do not prove a physical schema change. CREATE/ALTER statement counts provide the DDL evidence.
Initial earlier probe lacked SQL data because the mount path case differed from the autoload path; excluded from these results.

creation.method: Sequential fresh wiki creations through Special:CreateWiki; login and form preparation excluded. Provisioning completion observed every 500 ms.
creation.timing_clock: Host monotonic duration; queue/start times use Redis stream/status timestamps, with legacy Docker volume file timestamps as fallback.

findings: Bootstrap and normal passes both invoke core, extensions and stats update paths.
Normal pass loads 13 additional extensions/skins and registers two additional schema updates; UrlShortener registers addTable/addField for urlshortcodes.
Second pass executes four CREATE statements on every fresh fixture: three CheckUser cuci_* tables and urlshortcodes.

Bootstrap resolves virtual-checkuser-global to wikidb; normal runtime resolves it to the fixture database. LocalSettings uses array union when +wgVirtualDomainsMapping is already present, so its CheckUser mapping addition is ignored.
Most second-pass SQL text matches the first pass, but removing the pass would omit required configured schemas.
The built-in --initial flag seeds six legacy MySQL update keys; those do not cover the current core ALTER statements observed here. It is not a blanket fresh-install shortcut.
recommendation: Resolve the virtual-domain mapping mismatch first. Then prototype a single provisioning bootstrap that loads the actual per-wiki extension set/configuration, preserving setup-hook safety and validating full schema equivalence. Expected saved work is mostly the second process and duplicate checks (roughly a few tenths of a second), not the required first-pass DDL.
